description: Tests of the 7.4.11 suite that pass labels-off and do not pass in owners-user mode, the same in both worker modes.

categories.reason: A server in owner mode refuses CONFIG SET aof-use-rdb-preamble no, because the base of its append-only file is always a snapshot (see The append-only file in docs/persistence.md). The two tests of the other unit that switch the preamble off fail on that command. The suite applies the overrides of a server block that starts with the setting through CONFIG SET, so the refusal ends the block with an error that also ends its unit, and the tests of the block and every test after it do not run: in type/stream the two rewrite tests and the two help tests behind them, in type/stream-cgroups the first such block and every test after it, ten in all. The tests that rewrite, load or switch on the file with the preamble left on pass.

categories.reason: A login created without a clearance rule reads and writes only the lowest label (owner item A1), and a login without an owner rule acts as SHARED and has no operator scope, so such a login sees none of the data the suite's login writes as suite-user, INFO shows it no statistics, top-only commands such as CONFIG RESETSTAT are refused, a copy it writes is its own and cannot be changed or deleted by the suite's login, and its blocking pop waits on the name at its own label and owner, so a push by the suite's login never wakes it. The tests that authenticate as such a login differ; when one of them stops while its connection is still authenticated as that login, the later tests of the unit run there too, and the acl unit's 'blocked command gets rejected when reprocessed after permission change' waits for that wake until the unit times out, so its remaining tests do not run.

categories.reason: During CLIENT PAUSE WRITE a server with labels or owners on holds every EVALSHA until the pause ends, because whether a cached script is read-only would have to be looked up before the command's scope is known, and that lookup would tell one scope about another's cache (decision R11); owner mode turns that machinery on. The pause unit's test of a read-only EVALSHA under a write pause therefore waits for its reply until the suite reports no progress, which ends the unit, so the tests after it do not run.
